title: Auxiliary Power Unit Start Malfunction and Emergency Shutdown

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Abnormal procedure for an auxiliary power unit start that does not complete and for an emergency shutdown, including the case where the air inlet flap does not indicate open.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the crew procedure for an auxiliary power unit start that does not complete, for an automatic shutdown and for a manual emergency shutdown.
sections.description: Three malfunctions are covered. The first is a start that does not complete because the air inlet flap has not reached the open position, which the ECAM shows as APU FLAP NOT OPEN and which inhibits the start entirely; there is nothing the crew can do about it from the flight deck and the aircraft is dispatched on ground power or on a cross-bleed start. The second is a start that begins and then aborts, with the ECAM showing the reason; a second attempt is permitted after the unit has come to rest and the cooling period has elapsed, and a third attempt is not. The third is a fire indication, for which the shutdown is automatic on the ground and requires the crew to confirm and to discharge the bottle. The distinction between the first and second cases matters because they look similar from the crew seat and the maintenance response is entirely different.
sections.crew_procedure: If APU FLAP NOT OPEN is displayed: do not attempt a start. Enter the defect in the technical log with the outside air temperature and whether the aircraft was de-iced. Plan for ground power or a cross-bleed start. If the start aborts: MASTER SW OFF, wait for the page to show the unit stopped and the cooling period to elapse, then one further attempt is permitted. If APU FIRE is displayed on the ground: confirm the shutdown, discharge the bottle, and evacuate the area around the tail. In flight, follow the ECAM actions.
